title: Replication Study: Does Model Size Predict Safety Score?
original_idea: Run HELM Safety or AILuminate across the full scale range of one model family (e.g., Phi-3-mini 3.8B, Phi-3-small 7B, Phi-3-medium 14B). Plot safety score vs. parameter count and test whether the scaling relationship is monotonic.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If safety does not scale with model size, it challenges deployment intuitions. Useful but primarily descriptive.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Run one benchmark on 3 model sizes. Simple analysis. Medium compute covers up to 14B. Good beginner project.

narrow_scope.reasoning: One model family, one benchmark, one variable (size). Extremely focused.

novelty.reasoning: The Phi-3 technical report (arXiv:2404.14219) already provides safety evaluations across the Phi-3-mini (3.8B), Phi-3-small (7B), and Phi-3-medium (14B) family, including responsible AI benchmarks. HELM Safety v1.0 evaluates 24 models but does not present a systematic scaling analysis within a single family. Several studies note that safety does not scale monotonically with capability (e.g., inverse scaling results). The specific contribution — plotting safety vs. parameter count within one family on HELM/AILuminate — is a narrow replication that partially overlaps with existing technical reports but has not been published as a standalone analysis.
